questions.q: What is the core difference between hypothesis-driven hunting and exploratory (unstructured) hunting?
options: There is no real difference — both terms describe the same process
Exploratory hunting only runs scheduled analytics rules, while hypothesis-driven hunting never uses queries
Hypothesis-driven hunting starts from a specific, testable statement about attacker behavior; exploratory hunting browses logs without one
Hypothesis-driven hunting is only used by Microsoft's own security research team
questions.explain: Hypothesis-driven hunting writes down a specific, falsifiable statement before querying; exploratory hunting just browses data hoping something stands out.

questions.q: Why is "something bad might be happening on the network" not a usable hunting hypothesis?
options: It already describes a confirmed incident, not a hypothesis
It only applies to cloud environments, not on-premises networks
It isn't specific or testable — there's no query that could confirm or rule it out
It is too short to type into a KQL query editor
questions.explain: A usable hypothesis has to be specific enough that you know what evidence would confirm it, and testable against real log data.

questions.q: In the lesson's worked example, what makes rundll32.exe a LOLBin?
options: It's a legitimate, pre-installed Windows tool that an attacker repurposes maliciously because it's already trusted
It is malware that Microsoft ships disguised as a system tool
It only exists on domain controllers, never on regular workstations
It is a third-party tool that must be installed separately before it can be abused
questions.explain: LOLBin stands for Living-off-the-Land Binary — a legitimate tool attackers abuse precisely because it's already whitelisted and trusted.

questions.q: What specifically makes the rundll32.exe hypothesis in this lesson testable?
options: It is testable only after an incident has already been declared
It requires no log data at all to confirm
It names a specific binary, behavior, and reason, pointing directly at the process-creation fields an analyst would query
It can only be tested by Microsoft support engineers, not by SOC analysts
questions.explain: Because it names the exact process, field, and pattern to look for, it can be tested directly against process-creation log data.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which three sources do good hunting hypotheses typically come from?
options: Threat intelligence, the MITRE ATT&CK framework, and gaps found in past incidents
Random sampling of firewall logs, social media rumors, and vendor marketing
Exclusively from built-in Sentinel analytics rule templates
Only from automated machine learning models with no human input
questions.explain: Threat intel, ATT&CK techniques not yet hunted for, and lessons from past incidents are the three grounded sources this lesson names.
